events.comment: Samurai_Boss: every Samurai rule, shared by Samurai_Fight and Tutorial_Level. The scene links Player_Movement and Combat_Shared before this sheet. Tutorial_Level sets his Lives, UltMaxCasts and DebugInactive at scene start, before its link to this sheet.
Scene start: set the Samurai's walk speed and start his timers.

Samurai: keep his HP bar 3px above his head. Row 47 is the top of his head in the 96px frames, and his origin is at row 52.5, so the bar stays still between frames. The posture bar is fixed at the top of the screen.
Samurai: stay idle once the player is deleted.
Samurai: posture broke, so cancel its attack, including any wall slash or dash strike that has not landed yet.
Samurai: stun ended or deathblow landed, so go back to chasing.
Samurai: a lunge landed, so cancel whatever he is doing and flinch. A posture break, lost life or death from the same hit takes priority.
Samurai: the stagger ended, so go back to chasing.
Debug inactive (key 0): a stagger or stun just ended and sent him back to chasing, so stand idle again instead.
Samurai: count deflects during his swing combo. The third one plays the sword clash on top of the parry sound.
Third deflect of the combo: play the clash and start counting again.
Samurai recoil after a lunge stagger: slide away from the player for RecoilTime seconds, at RecoilSpeed.
Player on the right: slide left.
Player on the left: slide right.
Samurai: play its hit sound when it hits the player.
Stun: pause on the kneeling frame.
Stun: after KneelHold seconds, play the get-up frames.
Boss: final death. Play Samurai_Death, with two holds handled below, and leave the body on its last frame. Petals still out pop.
Death: pause on the settled kneeling frame, before he reaches for the blade.
Death: after DeathKneelHold seconds, carry on with the seppuku.
Death: pause with the blade drawn in, before he collapses.
Death: after DeathCutHold seconds, play the collapse.
Boss: lost a life, so start the intermission. Physics stay off during the taller petal animations, so the boss does not jump upward. Any petals still out pop.

Boss: at 75%, 50% and 25% HP on the last life, cast the ultimate. UltHpStep sets the HP gap and UltMaxCasts the number of casts. A hit that crosses two marks only triggers one cast. Locks the player, removes attacks still in flight, and starts the petal teleport instead of the cut.
Boss: dodged a hit. The first dodge of the fight always goes behind the player, later ones are random.

Boss: the player swings nearby, so maybe dodge that hit. DodgeChance and DodgeDelay control this. He cannot dodge during a stagger, while sheathing after a grab, during the petal cast, or while inactive from the debug key.
Boss: a lunge is coming in, so check once per lunge whether to dodge it. It starts too far away for the check above, which only runs on an attack press.
Same rules as a swing: DodgeChance and DodgeDelay control this, and no dodge during the petal cast or while inactive.
Boss offense: every GrabCooldown seconds, with the player within GrabTriggerRange, start a grab. GrabCount alternates the stab and the back stab.
Boss offense, phase 1: every PetalCooldown seconds, with the player at least PetalMinRange away, cast the petals. Skipped while petals from the last cast are still out.
Phase 1: PetalCountP1 petals over an arc of PetalArcP1 degrees above the player.
Phase 2: PetalCountP2 petals over an arc of PetalArcP2 degrees, a half circle around the player.
Player on the right: face right for the cast.
Player on the left: face left.
Every second grab is the back stab: he flash-steps to land in front of the player, facing them.
Boss offense: when the cooldown is ready and the player is far away, roll a new cooldown. On a successful roll, flash the eye glint before the dash strike. Otherwise keep walking.
Boss offense: the eye glint finished, so start the dash strike.
Aggressive phase, player at range: choose a skill.
Aggressive phase, player close: dash away, then choose a skill.
Aggressive phase: pick a Judgement Cut, the tornado or the petals at random. Two skills in a row without a tornado guarantee a tornado next.
Petals rolled while petals from the last cast are still out: use a Judgement Cut instead.
Combo: sometimes go to the far wall first, then cast the tornado and follow it with a dash.
Petals: cast them on the player.
Phase 1: PetalCountP1 petals over an arc of PetalArcP1 degrees above the player.
Phase 2: PetalCountP2 petals over an arc of PetalArcP2 degrees, a half circle around the player.
Player on the right: face right for the cast.
Player on the left: face left.

Flash step: halfway through vanishing, teleport and draw the trail, then face the player. The dash strike passes through the player and faces away. If a wall leaves no room, it lands in front and uses the crescent slash.
Back stab: land in front of the player, GrabPassStart away, for the tell.
Back stab: the player was caught, so land on their far side, GrabPassHold away.
Back stab finished: dash GrabPassExit away from the player, which hides the sheathe.
Grab: land close behind the player, on the side they are not facing.
Back stab: he lands facing away from the player, with the sword under his arm pointing at them.
Flash step finished: counter after going behind. After a dash away in the aggressive phase, choose a skill. After the combo dash, cast the tornado.
Grab: he has landed. Show the warning kanji over his head and start the tell, with the eye glint.
Back stab: he has landed behind the caught player, so stab. They are turned to face away from him, so the blade goes in through their back.
Back stab: the exit dash has landed. Wait in GrabRecover until the player is back up.
Grab tell: he can be hit here, and a posture break cancels the grab. Keep the kanji over his head and keep facing the player.
Keep the warning kanji centered above his head while it exists.
Remove the kanji if the grab was interrupted, by a stun, dodge, ultimate or debug key.
Grab tell over: one hand leaves the hilt and reaches for the player. Only a dodge or distance beats this, because the grab skips the deflect check.

Grab connects: the player is within GrabRange and not rolling or invulnerable. He seizes them, and they stand frozen in the idle pose until the blade goes in. For the back stab, the player is caught here and the flash-through follows.
Turn the player to face him, so they fall away from him.
Back stab: the player is caught, so flash through them. If a wall leaves no room behind them, this stays a normal stab.
Grab missed: he is left over-reached for GrabWhiffTime seconds, which is the punish window.
Grab missed: recover and go back to chasing.
Grab: he steps in to GrabHoldNow from the player before the stab, so the player is never pulled toward him.

parameters: (Player.CenterX() + sign(Samurai_NPC.CenterX() - Player.CenterX()) * Samurai_NPC.Variable(GrabHoldNow) - Samurai_NPC.CenterX()) * min(1, 25 * TimeDelta())

events.comment: Grab: the blade goes in. GrabDamage applies directly here, so the deflect check never sees it. The HP can be rallied back like any other hit.
The player only reacts now, as the blade goes in. Frame 4 of Player_Grabbed is the frame that matches the stab.
Grab: he rips the blade out.
Grab: the player hits the ground.
Back stab: the blade is out, so dash away. The player keeps falling, and the dash hides the sheathe.

Grab over: the player has got up, so free them. He may still be sheathing, or already gone after a back stab. From the normal stab, GrabRecover lets the sheathe finish. He can be hit during it, which makes it a small punish window.
He is still at the player, so let him finish.
Grab recovery: the sheathe has finished and the player is up, so go back to chasing.
Wall slash: the boss can be hit once the arrival streak ends. The stance and sword glint are the punish window.
Dash strike: spawn a hidden hitbox covering only the slash line, not his body.
Wall slash: spawn a hidden hitbox covering only the crescent, on the frames where it appears.
Dash strike finished: go back to chasing and start the dash cooldown from now.
Wall slash finished: go back to chasing and start the dash cooldown from now.
Dash strike: remove the line hitbox once the slash has faded.
Wall slash: remove the crescent hitbox when the crescent fades.
Dash strike and wall slash: remove the hidden hitbox if the attack was interrupted.
Quickdraw: on the draw frame, cut at the player position with a random variation, and play the Judgement Cut sound. Every second Quickdraw is a triple (below).

Triple Judgement Cut: every second Quickdraw casts TripleCuts cuts instead of one: this one on the player, then one to its left and one to its right. He holds his draw pose while the other two come out, TripleGap seconds apart.

Triple Judgement Cut: every TripleGap seconds, the next cut appears beside the first one: first to its left, then to its right. Each overlaps the middle cut by TripleOverlap (15%) of its width, so the three cover about 2.7 cuts' width and cannot be outrun. They are placed from where the player stood at the first cast (TripleX, TripleY), each with its own sound. A posture break or any change of state ends the Quickdraw, so the rest are cancelled.

parameters: Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleX) + (1 - 2 * Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleLeft)) * (1 - Samurai_NPC.Variable(TripleOverlap)) * Samurai_NPC.Variable(CutCirclePx) * Samurai_NPC.ScaleX() * Samurai_NPC.Variable(CutSizeMul)

events.comment: Last cut out: he finishes the Quickdraw animation, and the Quickdraw ends as usual.
Quickdraw finished: go back to chasing.
Tornado: on the release frame, send it the way the boss is facing (right).
Tornado: on the release frame, send it the way the boss is facing (left).
Tornado cast finished: go back to chasing. In the combo, flash the eye glint and follow up with the dash strike.
Petal cast: on frame PetalSpawnFrame, the blade has sunk into the ground, so create PetalCount petals at the player. Each one then waits for its slot below.
Create one petal per count. They start as "new" and are laid out by the next event.

Lay out each new petal around the player's body, where the player is right now. It stays at that spot. Slot 0 is the leftmost point of the arc above the player. Launches go left to right, PetalGap seconds apart, the first PetalFirstLaunch seconds after the spawn.
Petal cast: hold the open hand on frame PetalHoldFrame while the petals are waiting to launch. He does nothing else here and can be hit.
Petal cast hold: count the petals that have not launched yet. Any that burst early, for example on a deflect, no longer count.
Each petal still forming, hovering or glinting counts as waiting.
All petals have launched, so lower the arm.
Petal cast finished: go back to chasing, and start the skill and petal cooldowns from now.
Intermission: the petal burst ended, so hide and start the cuts.
Intermission: launch a cut at the player every 1.8 seconds, with the Judgement Cut sound. Each cut takes 1.7 seconds, so they do not overlap.
Intermission: all cuts finished, so reappear on the far side and switch to the aggressive phase.
Intermission finished: switch back to a normal-height animation, turn platformer physics back on, and start chasing.
Ultimate teleport: the Samurai has dissolved into petals, so the player does too, with their own animation. IsGrabbed keeps a deflect press or stray hit from replacing it until they reform.
Ultimate teleport: both are gone, so move them to mid-arena. The Samurai keeps the side he was on, UltStandoff away from the player. UltCenterX is the arena middle.
Ultimate teleport: start the player reforming, so both finish together.
Ultimate teleport: both have reformed, so give the player control of their deflect, bring back the bars, turn physics back on, and start the draw.
Ultimate: on the draw frame, cast Thousand Cuts on the player. The first slash lands on frame 13, and the rest follow every 3 frames.
Ultimate tell: on frame UltTellFrame, 0.32 seconds before the first slash, flash the gold kanji over the player with a sharp ring. Gold means it can be deflected, red means it cannot.
Ultimate tell: the first slash has landed, so remove the kanji.
Ultimate finished: unlock the player and go back to the aggressive phase.
Ultimate: allow a new hit between slashes. Slashes land on frames 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31, and 34. Uses mod() because GDevelop expressions have no % operator.
Move the tornado along the ground.
Tornado: loop its full-size frames while it crosses the arena.
Tornado: near the left edge, start the fade so it finishes at the wall.
Tornado: near the right edge, start the fade so it finishes at the wall.

Judgement Cut timing: each cut's frames follow judgement_cut.wav instead of a fixed speed. The circle appears on the boom and holds, the slash lines land on the sound's slashes, and the burst (frames 12 and 13, the only frames with a full hitbox) comes with the last slash at 1.40 s, so the cut hits once there. It then shatters and is removed at 1.70 s. Edit FRAMES to retime it.

inlineCode: // Judgement Cut timing, synced to judgement_cut.wav. Frame k shows from FRAMES[k] seconds after the cut appears.
const END = 1.7; // Seconds: the cut is removed here.

events.comment: Remove a Judgement Cut when its animation ends.
Remove the tornado when its animation ends.

Petals: until launch, stay in place and keep the tip pointing at the middle of the player's body. That is 77% down the player's frame, the middle of their collision mask (rows 43 to 80 of 80), the same in every animation. CenterY() would be the top of the head.
Petals: formed, so hover.
Petals: PetalGlintTime seconds before launch, the edge glints red. This is the tell for each petal.
Petals: launch at LaunchAt, along the direction the petal points, which is at where the player is right now. It flies straight from here and stops tracking.
Petals: fly in a straight line.
Petals: hit the player or deflected, so burst. Combat_Shared sets HasHit for both.
Petals: missed and reached the ground or a wall, so burst there.
Petals: safety net. Burst any petal still flying 3 seconds after its launch time.
Petals: the player is gone, so burst every petal that is still out.

Petals: a bursting petal comes apart into blossom petals. Create the pop where it was, at the same size and never rotated, so the petals always drift and sink downward, then remove the blade. One at a time, so two bursting on the same frame both get a pop.
Petal pop: remove it when its animation ends.
Remove the ultimate when its animation ends.
Ultimate effect: the scenery goes grey except inside the cut, fading in and out. Ground_Stuff is on the Background layer so it greys too, while the player and samurai stay in color.

inlineCode: // Ultimate effect: turns the Background layer grey, except for a colored circle at the cut.
const ULT_RADIUS = 198; // Circle radius in the image (66) times the object scale (3).
state = runtimeScene.__ultGrey = { amount: 0, flash: 0, lastFrame: -1, x: 0, y: 0, radius: 0, filter: null };
"precision highp float; // Must match the default vertex shader, or the shader fails and the layer disappears.",
"  float outside = smoothstep(uRadius - 3.0, uRadius + 3.0, distance(position, uCenter));",
state.filter = new PIXI.Filter(undefined, fragment, { uCenter: new Float32Array(2), uRadius: 0, uAmount: 0, uFlash: 0 });

events.comment: Remove the dash trail after 0.2 seconds.
Samurai_Idle Rules
Samurai_Waiting Rules
Samurai_AggroReady Rules
Close enough: start attacking. AttackRange is the same distance the follow-up check uses after each swing.
Samurai_Attacking Rules
First swing of a combo: start the deflect count over.
Swing: hold the raised sword for SwingPause seconds. The wait is the same every swing, so the rhythm can be learned.
Swing: after SwingPause seconds, release the sword and create the hitbox.

Swing finished, combo not over: if the player is behind the samurai or out of AttackRange, skip the next swing and go back to AggroReady to close the gap. ComboCount is kept, so the 3-swing limit still leads to Cooldown.
Samurai_Cooldown
Debug: F7 cancels whatever the Samurai is doing and casts the tornado at the player. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release.

Debug: F2 (without Shift) casts a Judgement Cut on the player right away, the same cut as his Quickdraw (size, damage and sound), to test its timing. The Samurai keeps doing whatever he was doing. Remove before release.

Debug: Shift+F2 cancels whatever the Samurai is doing and starts a triple Quickdraw: QuickdrawCount is set so this draw is a triple. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release.

Debug: F6 cancels whatever the Samurai is doing and casts the petals at the player, with the count for the current phase. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab, or while petals are still out. Remove before release.

Debug: 0 toggles the Samurai inactive for simple checks. He stops what he is doing and stands idle, but can still be hit, staggered and posture-broken. Turning him on is ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release.
Inactive: switch him back on and let him chase again.
Active: cancel whatever he is doing, including a flash step that hid him or a held petal cast, and stand idle. Petals already out keep going.
Clear the flag so the next press toggles again.
Phase 1: PetalCountP1 petals over an arc of PetalArcP1 degrees above the player.
Phase 2: PetalCountP2 petals over an arc of PetalArcP2 degrees, a half circle around the player.
Player on the right: face right for the cast.
Player on the left: face left.
Debug: F8 cancels whatever the Samurai is doing and starts the grab. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release.
Every second grab is the back stab: he flash-steps to land in front of the player, facing them.

Debug: F9 puts the Samurai on his last life just under 75% HP, which starts the ultimate. Press it again later to repeat it. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove this before release.

parameters: "Lives: " + ToString(Player.Variable(Lives)) + NewLine() + "Dist: " + ToString(round(Samurai_NPC.Distance(Player))) + NewLine() + "Player HP: " + ToString(Player.Variable(Health)) + " | Posture: " + ToString(round(Player.Variable(Posture))) + " (" + ToString(Player.Variable(IsPostureBroken)) + ")" + NewLine() + "Samurai HP: " + ToString(Samurai_NPC.Variable(Health)) + " | Posture: " + ToString(round(Samurai_NPC.Variable(Posture))) + " (" + ToString(Samurai_NPC.Variable(IsPostureBroken)) + ")" + NewLine() + "Samurai AI: " + Samurai_NPC.VariableString(AIState) + " | SubState: " + ToString(Samurai_NPC.Variable(AttackSubState)) + " | Combo: " + ToString(Samurai_NPC.Variable(ComboCount)) + NewLine() + "Iframe: " + ToString(Player.Variable(Iframe)) + NewLine() + "Stamina: " + ToString(round(Player.Variable(Stamina))) + " / " + ToString(Player.Variable(MaxStamina))
